$comment: ★ SHIPS THE TWO FUNCTIONS, DELIBERATELY SHIPS NO MIB CONSTANTS — the two halves have DIFFERENT reasons and neither is an oversight. Neutral shipped <sys/sysctl.h> (Darwin/BSD), added by the SQLite-CLI-for-arm64-Darwin cycle. ★★ (1) WHY THE FUNCTIONS ARE NOW HERE — THIS FILE USED TO ARGUE THE OPPOSITE AND THE ARGUMENT WAS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. The previous version shipped NO `symbols` and justified it thus: the functions 'are already shipped ... re-declaring either here would plant a SECOND eager import of the same symbol for no gain'. THAT IS WRONG IN EFFECT, because DESCRIPTOR VISIBILITY IS PER-HEADER: a descriptor SHADOWS the real header TOTALLY, and the angle-include funnel resolves DESCRIPTOR FIRST (src/core/types/include_path_resolve.hpp:205-224 — priority 1 Descriptor, 2 Source, 3 NotFound; it keys on descriptor-FILE existence ALONE, and an existing-but-format-unavailable descriptor STILL returns Descriptor rather than falling through to a real header). So a TU that includes <sys/sysctl.h> sees THIS FILE AND NOTHING ELSE — unistd.json's rows are not in scope for it, however much they exist. MEASURED 2026-08-05 in the staged tree (/home/rafael/src/sqlite/bld-dss/sqlite3.c, re-checked this cycle rather than inherited): `#include <sys/sysctl.h>` at :28198, the call `sysctlbyname("hw.ncpu", &cpuCount, &len, NULL, 0)` at :28388, and the nearest later <unistd.h> at :31315 (inside a conditional) with the first unconditional one at :39635 — BOTH thousands of lines AFTER the call, so neither can rescue it. MEASURED both directions with the real CLI the same day: <sys/sysctl.h> + a sysctlbyname call failed `error[S0001] got sysctlbyname` on BOTH macho targets, while the identical call under <unistd.h> compiled rc=0 — the header, not the symbol, was the variable. NOTE the line numbers above are true for the tree staged on that date only; the harness re-pulls upstream every run, so re-measure before re-quoting. What does NOT drift is the ORDER, and the order is the whole defect. ★ (2) WHY A BYTE-IDENTICAL DUPLICATE IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND NOT A SMELL: the two rows below are copied VERBATIM from unistd.json:42-43 — same signature spelling, same kind/linkage, same [macho] gate, same column padding. Cross-descriptor duplicates dedupe by NAME first-wins, so a byte-identical duplicate resolves to exactly ONE thing no matter which header a TU includes first (sqlite3.c includes both), while a DIVERGENT duplicate is the case that fails loud — project rule #47, a shared declaration must resolve identically per target. Keeping them literally identical IS the requirement: ANY future edit to either row must be applied to BOTH. The `library` map is declared here for the same anti-drift reason: unistd.json states `{elf: libc.so.6, macho: /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib}` EXPLICITLY, whereas an absent map inherits the LANGUAGE default (the `externLibraryByFormat` map in src/dss-config/sources/c-subset.lang.json — its `macho` row is /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib, MEASURED identical today; cited BY KEY rather than by line: the citation this replaces was a bare filename plus a line number, which named no directory and pointed at the map's `pe` row rather than the `macho` row it was arguing about — a key spelling survives both problems), so stating it makes the two descriptors agree BY STATEMENT rather than by coincidence and a later change to that default cannot silently split them. EXPORT-VERIFIED, which under the eager-import law is the load-bearing check (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT: an unexported name breaks EVERY macho binary's LOAD, not merely this header's users): both names were confirmed present in libSystem by a real dlopen+dlsym run on an actual Mac (.plans/_deferred-anchor-registry.md:740) — this ships NO name that has not been seen on a real Mac. An `includes: ["unistd.h"]` transitive pull was the alternative considered and REJECTED: it would drag all 36 unistd symbols into the eager-import set of every TU that includes <sys/sysctl.h>. ★★ (3) THE MIB CONSTANTS STAY UNSHIPPED, and that half of the old comment stands unchanged. THE CORPUS USAGE, MEASURED not inherited: a grep over the whole staged tree finds `src/test1.c:9100-9103` using the MIB-ARRAY form (`nm[0] = CTL_HW; nm[1] = HW_AVAILCPU;` then `nm[1] = HW_NCPU;`). THE CLI IS UNAFFECTED — sqlite3.c uses the NAME-based `sysctlbyname` above, which needs no constant at all, and `shell.c` references none. THE TESTFIXTURE IS AFFECTED: a macho build of `src/test1.c` will fail LOUD (S0001, undefined `CTL_HW`/`HW_AVAILCPU`/`HW_NCPU`) the moment it is attempted, for exactly the shadowing reason spelled out in (1). That is a fail-loud gap, not a silent one, and it is the named in-tree consumer that gives D-FFI-DARWIN-SYSCTL-CONSTANTS-EMPTY its priority. WE STILL CANNOT MEASURE THE VALUES: the SDK slice this work had (/tmp/apple_sdk_probe/MacOSX26.4.sdk/usr/include) carries only sys/{fcntl,file,mount,param,syslimits}.h + malloc/malloc.h — sys/sysctl.h is NOT in it. The CTL_* namespace is 4.4BSD-derived and *looks* portable, which is exactly what makes guessing it dangerous: because the descriptor shadows the real header even on a NATIVE macOS host (where the SDK header would otherwise be used via D-INCLUDE-ANGLE-SOURCE-FALLBACK), a wrong MIB constant would NOT fail to compile — it would query the WRONG kernel node at runtime and return a plausible number. A partial-but-correct surface is a fail-loud gap; a complete-but-guessed surface is a silent wrong answer. We take the gap and ANCHOR it: D-FFI-DARWIN-SYSCTL-CONSTANTS-EMPTY (closing work: measure CTL_*/HW_*/KERN_* + `struct sysctl_oid`-adjacent shapes against a real SDK, then ship the closed domains whole). ★ THE MACRO: `_SYS_SYSCTL_H_` is the include guard, the one declaration the real header unambiguously makes and that no consumer branches on. It is no longer load-bearing for shipping (the loader refuses a descriptor that declares NOTHING — shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp:2188-2199 — and the `symbols` above now satisfy that on their own), but it remains correct and is kept. The name follows the Darwin `_SYS_<NAME>_H_` convention MEASURED across every sibling in the slice (sys/mount.h → _SYS_MOUNT_H_, sys/param.h → _SYS_PARAM_H_, sys/file.h → _SYS_FILE_H_, sys/fcntl.h → _SYS_FCNTL_H_, sys/syslimits.h → _SYS_SYSLIMITS_H_) — the convention is measured, this specific name is INFERRED from it. Gated availableObjectFormats:[macho] — an elf/pe #include fails loud (the windows.json:5 [pe] precedent, inverted); Linux's sysctl(2) is deprecated and its MIB values differ, so an elf build must never silently pick this up.
